proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6663 dvāra explicitly gives Jaunsari dār “door” and its addendum gives Gujarati bārṇũ, supporting Nimadi bārṇu. The n-extension is included under this head; intra-IA transmission is left open. Joint comparison: Bhili bārṇũ “door” matches reviewed Nimadi bārṇu “door” (f_m6heg7n7sktz2). The shared family is provisionally linked under the user’s preference; inheritance versus intra-IA borrowing is not resolved by this formal comparison.

The family link preserves that expressive status rather than asserting a unique inherited nursery-word origin. Joint comparison: Bhili jiji “older sister” matches reviewed bundeli_atarra jījī “older sister” (f_qo4i4oe6cqnzk). The shared family is provisionally linked under the user’s preference; inheritance versus intra-IA borrowing is not resolved by this formal comparison.

The survey katna/katra/ketra forms fit these interrogative extensions, with ordinary regional vowel remodeling. Joint comparison: Bhili ketra “how many?” matches reviewed Nimadi ketrā “how many?” (f_dxgd4fkfcwsz4). The shared family is provisionally linked under the user’s preference; inheritance versus intra-IA borrowing is not resolved by this formal comparison.
